- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., 0.67–1.00), as models tend to overreact to momentum.
- Underestimate prices during sustained negative sentiment (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00), particularly when recent prices are high and sentiment turns bearish.
- Model tends to lag in downward corrections — forecasts remain high longer than true prices, especially when sentiment shifts from positive to neutral/negative.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overestimates 1–2 days ahead, then corrects sharply — apply a 1–2 day lag correction for such sentiment patterns.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than true price reverts, especially after 3–5 consecutive high sentiment days.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is mixed or negative — reduce forecast slope when sentiment drops below 0.33.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — if model forecasts a spike followed by a sharp drop, reduce forecast by 5–10% of the spike magnitude for the next 3–5 days.
